### Introduction:

This time you will create the data.

***Exercise based on [Chris Albon](http://chrisalbon.com/) work, the credits belong to him.***

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Step 2. Create the DataFrame with the data below. The columns should be in this order: first_name, last_name, age, female, preTestScore, postTestScore.

```{r given-data}
raw_data <- list(
  first_name = c("Jason", "Molly", "Tina", "Jake", "Amy"),
  last_name = c("Miller", "Jacobson", "Ali", "Milner", "Cooze"),
  female = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 1),
  age = c(42, 52, 36, 24, 73),
  preTestScore = c(4, 24, 31, 2, 3),
  postTestScore = c(25, 94, 57, 62, 70)
)
```

```{r}
df <- as_tibble(raw_data) |>
  select(first_name, last_name, age, female, preTestScore, postTestScore)

df
```

### Step 3. Create a Scatterplot of preTestScore and postTestScore, with the size of each point determined by age

#### Hint: Don't forget to place the labels

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = preTestScore, y = postTestScore, size = age)) +
  geom_point() +
  # set labels and titles
  labs(title = "preTestScore x postTestScore", x = "preTestScore", y = "postTestScore")
```

### Step 4. Create a Scatterplot of preTestScore and postTestScore.

### This time the size should be 4.5 times the postTestScore and the color determined by sex

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = preTestScore, y = postTestScore,
               size = postTestScore * 4.5, color = factor(female))) +
  geom_point() +
  # set labels and titles
  labs(title = "preTestScore x postTestScore", x = "preTestScore", y = "postTestScore",
       size = "postTestScore x 4.5", color = "female")
```
